name: module-readme-parity
question: Does every module README's File Index match the files actually in that directory?

assertion.asserts: every module directory's README.md File Index names exactly the files that are really there, so an agent orienting from the README is never misled
assertion.measures: for every directory holding a git-tracked README.md with a heading matching '## File Index' or '## 2. File Index', the backtick-quoted filenames in that section's body, diffed against the direct-child git-tracked files of that directory (README.md itself excluded); separately, a directory with >= 3 tracked source files and NO README.md at all is reported as a presence gap (RB-44's other half of today's module-index)
known_gaps: scope is git-tracked files only (uldf.git.ls_files) -- an untracked file is invisible to both the parity and the presence checks, which is deliberate: a build artifact directory (bin/obj, node_modules) is normally gitignored and never reaches either check.

the File Index heading match is textual (a regex over the heading line), not a markdown parser -- a heading spelled some third way is not recognized and that README is silently outside the parity check (it would still count for the presence check as 'has a README', so it is never double-penalized).

'source file' for the presence half is a fixed extension list; a directory of three README-only or config-only files is never flagged, and a real module in an unlisted language is invisible to the presence check specifically.
existence, not correctness: an index entry naming a file that exists passes even if the file's actual purpose no longer matches the index's one-line description -- this oracle cannot see content.

a backticked token in a File Index counts as a claim about a file only if it names a tracked file that is there, or carries an extension one of that directory's own tracked files uses; an existing subdirectory is dropped, and everything else is read as the prose a File Index also contains (identifiers, literals, call sites). The gap this buys is a stale entry that no longer resembles anything in its directory: the LAST file of its extension, and any name with no extension at all (`Makefile`, `LICENSE`, `Dockerfile` where no sibling is extensionless). Both are invisible; a file that is really there is never missed, whatever it is called. It replaces the opposite failure, measured 2026-09-07: `""`, `0`, `=`, `<table>`, `#[ignore]`, `.await`, `CELL_IDS` and `page.goto` were all reported as files that are gone -- 24 from `hooks/README.md` alone, and enough across five instrumented projects to hold proof (3) red on nothing.
